shorts.description:
I was talking to a friend of mine who decided recently to get into the content game.

He asked why my content was getting more reach than his.

I said “I don’t know. We put out about 250 per week. How many pieces a week are you putting out?”

He replied “I’m posting a measly once a day. Ha! Thank you for resetting my minimum standard.”

He’s already an incredibly successful man (more than me) and it instantly clicked for him. 

Volume. (But there’s more to it than that)

I’ve had this happen to me in business more times than I can count.

I think “oh I should just do 30% more or 50% more.”

But the people who are beating me aren’t doing 50 PERCENT more, they’re doing 50 TIMES more. Big. Difference.

We think we’re doing something wrong, but in reality we aren’t doing nearly enough of it.

To get 5x the results sometimes you have to put in 50x the effort.
shorts.title: You're Posting Once. I Was Posting 60 Times a Day.

shorts.description:
If you have no money, you should have no shame.

Knock.
Call.
Email.
Text. 
DM.
Ask. 

Life-changing doors don’t open themselves.
shorts.title: If You Have No Money, You Have No Shame

shorts.description:
Instead of the S&P 500, most should invest in the S&Me 500.

10x what you make rather than earning 10% on what you’ve made.
shorts.title: Nothing Has a Higher ROI Than Your Ability to Earn

shorts.description: We stay poor until we’ve learned all the lessons poverty has to teach.
shorts.title: How To Stay Poor

shorts.description:
Beginners overvalue thinking and undervalue doing—

—Advanced do the opposite.
shorts.title: How I Cut Training By 90%

shorts.description: If you’re good at business, you make more money doing the opportunity than selling it.
shorts.title: You're Sitting on a $5M Business and Doing Surgery for the Same Pay

shorts.description:
One of the first questions I ask when we invest in a company is: 

“What’s stopping us from doing 10x more of what’s currently working?”

Oftentimes: nothing.
shorts.title: How to talk to staff that don’t want to sell

shorts.description: Pain and time are the only two things that stand between everyone and what they want.
shorts.title: These 2 Questions Will Make Them Buy

shorts.description:
Most people aren’t that good. 
They make one VSL and never edit it with obvious fixes. 
They don’t look at screen recordings to edit their pages. 
They don’t script out hooks.
They don’t make enough ads.
They don’t review sales calls.

Beating them isn’t hard if you actually try.
shorts.title: How I Make 750 Ads From One Filming Session

shorts.description: The largest gains in operational efficiency come from realizing something’s not worth doing anymore.
shorts.title: Don’t Use AI Until You’ve Watched This

shorts.description:
4 paths to mega money:

1) Bet other people’s money on other people’s businesses (fund managers)

2) Bet your money on other people’s businesses (investing)

3) Bet other people’s money on your business (raising funds)

4) Bet your money on your own business (bootstrapping).
shorts.title: There Are Only 4 Paths to Becoming Ultra Wealthy

shorts.description:
All new businesses have debt. It’s guaranteed. It’s just not always financial debt…you can have:

Talent debt
Process debt
Management debt
Technical debt
Cultural debt
Brand debt

You should take on the debt you think will be easiest to pay back when it comes due (with interest)
shorts.title: He Did 600 Interviews to Find His Cofounder

shorts.description:
The reason you’re confused about what opportunity to pursue is that your only goal is to make money. 

And since there are so many ways to do it, you can’t figure out which one to pick.

Fix: Figure out what you wanna DO. Then within that context, which version makes you money.
shorts.title: Why You Can't Pick a Business to Start

shorts.description:
The other great reason for working harder is:

The harder you work the more you realize what you used to think was hard work, is not even close to what you’re capable of.
shorts.title: You’ll See This When You’re Going Through a Hard Time

shorts.description: You’re not making as much money as you want because you’re not as good as you think you are.
shorts.title: “Why Am I Still Broke?”

suck at something

wait until people ask for free work and you can't take them on
now you have more demand than you have supply
begin to charge money

congrats. u hav business

shorts.description:
I believe the hardest decision in entrepreneurship is knowing when to give up.

The question is whether the lack of desired success is due to impatience, poor execution, or an opportunity not worth pursuing. 

Imo it’s the decision that requires the most discernment in the game.
shorts.title: This Thing Doesn't Have Value. That Thing Does.

shorts.description: People are always willing to pay you significantly more if you ask for payment out of money you help them make.
shorts.title: The Future of Work Is Coming In as an Entire Department

shorts.description: More people lose from fear of failure than actual failure.
shorts.title: Fear Is a Mile Wide and an Inch Deep

shorts.description:
Affiliates in a nutshell:

1) Figure out who has your audience
2) Figure out what they want more than anything
3) Give it to them, then ask them if they’d be willing to share something that benefits them - and their audience - that happens to help you.
shorts.title: You Probably Need Wealthier Affiliates

shorts.description:
Contrary to popular belief, older business owners don’t just hand over their profitable businesses when they retire. 

But they will give you their headaches and debts for $0 down.

Just because it doesn’t cost money doesn’t mean it’s free.
shorts.title: Ask Your Dad for the Business Instead of a Salary

shorts.description:
The fastest path to $10M is often not the fastest path to $100m.

In this way, patience is strategy.
shorts.title: You're Shooting Yourself in the Foot Trying to Go $2M to $100M in 12 Months

shorts.description: The single greatest skill you can develop is the ability to stay in a great mood in the absence of things to be in a great mood about.
shorts.title: Be in a Good Mood for No Reason

shorts.description:
Had a convo with a young founder who was “stuck” this morning. 

Here was my parting advice:

1) Change directions less. 
2) Stick with things long enough to see if it really worked. And if you don’t know yet. Then keep doing it. 
3) The more stable you are the more stable your team will be
4) You can attract and retain talent proportional to your personal growth
5) Your business is simple, don’t complicate it.
6) Focusing on getting better will make you bigger. But focusing on getting bigger will only spread you to thin.
7) Raise your people standards. 
8) Build from the customer backwards to money, not the other way around.
9) Remember you’re gonna die and it’s not gonna matter so don’t stress so much - you’ve already won.
shorts.title: You Didn't Build It, So Respect the People Who Did

shorts.description:
When someone goes out of their way to personally wrong you, you only have one move left—win anyways.

Because for the rest of time…you get to be you and they have to be them. 

No fairer justice exists.
shorts.title: You Only Get Money Back If They Have It

shorts.description:
If you make content, some people will find a way to hate you for it. 

This is a cost of doing business. Reminder: almost every major prophet was murdered - public sentiment is a poor short term gauge for human value (See: Jesus).

1) People create straw men: "if you tell me I should focus on long term bets you're telling me I should NEVER enjoy my life"

2) You will become more interesting than smaller creators, and negative hooks create drama, so bad creators will make negative hooks about you because they don't know how to gather attention on their own.

3) Media is consumed in short snippets. 99% of people will never consume more than one angle - then derive an almost entirely self-generated opinion of you. This means most people will literally never understand you. IT also means that the praise and boos have equivalent value - zero.

TLDR: You cannot demand people have infinite context in a world that offers none.
shorts.title: The Criticism Is a Fixed Cost Either Way

shorts.description:
Let me save you a bunch of headache: 
If someone steals from you and promises they won’t. They’re lying, they’ll steal again…just more effectively.

And even if they never do, there are buckets of other great people you can choose from without that track record.

Cut and move on
shorts.title: It's Not the First Time They Stole, It's the First Time You Caught Them

shorts.description:
Most entrepreneurs can’t help themselves…

When business growth slows, they think ‘What’s something new I can sell my audience?’

Rather than, ‘How I do the hard thing and keep growing my main thing?’

New doesn’t compound.

Better questions better answers.
shorts.title: Your Business Isn't Unscalable, It's Just Hard

shorts.description: To increase sales, get everyone on your team to follow the script.
shorts.title: When I Fire These People, The Whole Team Steps Up

shorts.description:
Advice to younger dudes on finding a “keeper”:

Watch how they handle bad days.

Anyone can be in love when things are easy. But life is hard. You want someone who can handle it. 

It’s easier to find romance than resilience.
shorts.title: Give Her a Try Before You Buy

shorts.description:
How to identify business bottlenecks: 

Look at everything on your calendar. 

Everything you see is what needs to get removed for you to go to the next level.
shorts.title: You're the Bottleneck — Here's the Fix

shorts.description: Building a $1,000,000 Business for a Stranger in 56 Mins
shorts.title: Marry Her Now and Save $740,000 in Taxes

shorts.description:
Most entrepreneurs can’t help themselves…

When business growth slows, they think ‘What’s something new I can sell my audience?’

Rather than, ‘How I do the hard thing and keep growing my main thing?’

New doesn’t compound.

Better questions better answers.

shorts.description:
If you make your team’s default timeline for projects and tasks “end of day” instead of “end of week” you move seven times faster.

And it starts with you.

Speed is king.
shorts.title: End Every Meeting With This: Who, What, When

shorts.description:
A big influencer made an off handed content about our shorts. He said "you guys are masters." It shocked me because all we do is:
1) Post a lot of sh*t without worrying about duds
2) Do more until it stops working.
3) Then try more stuff til we find something else. 
That's it.
shorts.title: Give Contractors a Rebate to Fund All Your Content

shorts.description:
The fastest path to $10M is often not the fastest path to $100m.

In this way, patience is strategy.
shorts.title: You're Stopping Yourself by Trying to Do It Too Fast

shorts.description:
If you’re brand new to business, and don’t know how to divide your time, consider a 4-4-4 split:

4hrs promotion: let people know about your stuff

4hrs delivery: give them what u promised

4hrs building: figuring out what to do next and how to do it.

Promote. Deliver. Build.
shorts.title: No One Knows You Exist. That's the Issue.

shorts.description:
In my experience, people buy because of how crisply you articulate their problems to them, not, the benefits of your solution.

The goal is for them to feel understood more than to understand your products/services.
shorts.title: Good Writing Is That Someone Understands. Good Copy Is That People Feel Understood.

shorts.description:
In my experience, people buy because of how crisply you articulate their problems to them, not, the benefits of your solution.

The goal is for them to feel understood more than to understand your products/services.
shorts.title: People Believe Nothing You Say and Everything They Say

shorts.description:
Imagine every past customer still paid you today—how big would your business be?

Once I understood this, I understood how to build a big business.

It takes time. And I had to focus on making stuff people keep buying.

This way effort stacks rather than restarting monthly.
shorts.title: How to Make $100K in 4 Days Without Destroying Your Reputation

shorts.description: Business is surprisingly simple but deceptively hard. On a long enough time horizon, the only thing that matters is making a product everyone loves. If you did only that, you'd beat just about everyone.
shorts.title: Your Promotion and Delivery Are the Same Thing

shorts.description:
Imagine you define success as whatever you want.

Then imagine living that.

Understanding that it’s a single player playing a game they define the rules to, against themselves.

Best part: you can change the rules.
shorts.title: There's No Mariachi Band Coming for You

shorts.description:
Entrepreneurs get held back by people in their lives who think entrepreneurs should somehow lead the same life as them but somehow get a different outcome.

Mediocre in. Mediocre out.
shorts.title: You Don't Want Their Life, So Why Listen to Their Opinion?

shorts.description:
The biggest misconception I had when starting a business was that I would somehow “know enough” to be ready. 

You never will. You have to learn how to operate off incomplete information - with conviction. Start. Then adjust as you learn more. That’s it.
shorts.title: Stop Waiting for the Right Time, Wait for the Right Conditions

shorts.description:
Pricing is the single strongest lever on profit in a business.

And yet - 95% of business owners look at what everyone else is charging, take the average, make that their price and never think about it again.

The problem is - the business owners they’re copying are broke too.
shorts.title: The Perfect Price Is the Maximum a Customer Will Spend

shorts.description:
The single greatest change in my life came from doing one thing:

Ignoring people’s advice who didn't have what I wanted.

This includes parents, friends, acquaintances, and random posts I see on my newsfeed.

The world got quieter, and that made decisions a lot easier.
shorts.title: The Day I Wake Up and Realize I'm Wrong, I'll Change

shorts.description:
The most common constraint for business growth isn't access to capital but allocation of attention.

You don't need more money, you need fewer things to focus on.
shorts.title: Only Focus on the Rate Limiter

shorts.description:
Most people never start making money because they can’t even admit that they suck. 

They stay stuck in the delusion that they somehow have an amazing product that no one wants and no one talks about.

If you were the best, you’d be making money.

So. You’re not. Now work.
shorts.title: You Thinking You're Working Is Getting In The Way Of You Actually Working
